verdict.rationale: The only webhook evidence is a single security-doc mention that requests sent from Honeybadger servers for "web hooks" carry a secret Honeybadger-Token header. That confirms outbound webhooks exist and can be authenticated, but nothing shows how to subscribe or configure them. Missing for 10: documentation of webhook setup/subscription, list of subscribable event types (errors, deploys, uptime, alarms), payload schema, retry/delivery semantics, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
